verdict.rationale: The runtime probe records the core engine as MIT-licensed on npm, which carries no per-game fees that could be repriced. The pricing page says games you create 'will still work — they are not linked to the licence' and grants full commercial rights, so shipped games are structurally insulated from later pricing changes. However, nothing in the pack shows a history of stable pricing or license terms, which is the 'track record' the story asks for. Missing for 10: documented history of pricing/licence changes (or their absence), an explicit commitment against retroactive changes, independent/community corroboration of licensing stability.
